python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# Individual income tax receipts (net of refunds) for FY 1929-1942
# Data from treasury_bulletin_1942_07_page_76.txt
# These are in thousands of dollars, convert to billions

years = np.array([1929, 1930, 1931, 1932, 1933, 1934, 1935, 1936, 1937, 1938, 1939, 1940, 1941, 1942])

# Individual income tax receipts in thousands of dollars
receipts_thousands = np.array([
    1095541,  # 1929
    1146845,  # 1930
    833648,   # 1931
    427191,   # 1932
    352573,   # 1933
    419509,   # 1934
    527113,   # 1935
    674416,   # 1936
    1091741,  # 1937
    1286312,  # 1938
    1028834,  # 1939
    982017,   # 1940
    1417655,  # 1941
    3262800   # 1942
])

# Convert to billions of dollars
receipts = receipts_thousands / 1_000_000

print("Data (Year, Receipts in billions):")
for y, r in zip(years, receipts):
    print(f"  {y}: {r:.6f}")

# Perform OLS regression
# Using normal equations: beta = (X'X)^-1 X'y
X = np.vstack([np.ones(len(years)), years]).T
beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, receipts, rcond=None)[0]

intercept, slope = beta
print(f"\nOLS Regression:")
print(f"  Intercept: {intercept:.6f}")
print(f"  Slope: {slope:.6f}")

# Project to year 2000
year_2000 = 2000
projected_2000 = intercept + slope * year_2000
print(f"\nProjected for FY 2000: {projected_2000:.6f} billion dollars")

# Actual FY 2000 net individual income tax receipts
# From treasury_bulletin_2001_12_page_17.txt
# "Net" column under Income taxes = 1,004,461 million = 1004.461 billion
actual_2000 = 1004461 / 1000  # Convert millions to billions
print(f"Actual FY 2000: {actual_2000:.6f} billion dollars")

# Difference
difference = actual_2000 - projected_2000
print(f"\nDifference (actual - projected): {difference:.6f} billion dollars")
print(f"Rounded to nearest tenth: {round(difference, 1)}")

EOF
